title: Three Nights at Thawr
reader_question: How did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr stay hidden in the cave at Thawr while Quraysh hunted for them?

overview.text: The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr had slipped out of Makkah by night, heading not north to Madinah but south, to a mountain called Thawr. There, in a cave, they would wait three nights. By morning Quraysh would know he was gone, and they would send riders in every direction, with a great reward for whoever brought him back. Everything now depended on a handful of people who knew where they were, and on what the searchers would see when they reached the mountain.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr could not walk calmly beside him. He kept moving, at times ahead of the Prophet ﷺ and at times behind him, until the Prophet ﷺ asked why. "Messenger of Allah," he said, "I think of those coming after you, and walk behind you; then I think of those lying in wait, and walk in front of you." ‘Umar would later say that this one night of Abu Bakr's was better than the whole family of ‘Umar.

paragraphs.text: About five miles south of Makkah they reached Mount Thawr, and a cave in it, an opening in the mountainside. They came to it at night. "Stay where you are, Messenger of Allah," Abu Bakr said, "until I have checked the cave for you." He went in first and felt his way around it, to see whether a wild animal or a snake was inside, ready to take the harm himself. Then the Prophet ﷺ came in after him. For three nights, this would be their hiding place.

Quraysh offered a hundred camels to whoever brought him back to them. paragraphs.text: Later Abu Bakr's father, Abu Quhafah, came to the house. He had lost his sight. "By Allah," he said, "I think he has hurt you with his money as well as himself." "No, father," said Asma. "He has left us plenty." She took some stones, put them in the niche where her father had kept his money, laid a cloth over them, and took the old man's hand. "Father, put your hand on this money." He felt it. "No harm, then. If he has left you this, he has done well; this is enough for you." "By Allah," Asma said, "he had left us nothing. I only wanted to calm the old man."

paragraphs.text: Others followed the Prophet's ﷺ tracks out of the city. At the mountain the trail became confused, so they climbed it, and passed by the cave. They came right above it, close enough for the two inside to hear their voices. Abu Bakr looked up and saw their feet over his head. "Messenger of Allah," he said, "if one of them looked at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet." The Prophet ﷺ answered: "Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?"

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr was overcome with worry and fear. The Prophet ﷺ told him, "Do not grieve; Allah is with us," and he prayed, and calm from Allah came down on him. The searchers saw a spider's web across the entrance and said, "If anyone had gone in here, there would be no spider's web over its entrance." Allah blinded their eyes to him, and at last the searchers gave up and went back.

Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him, and supported him with forces you did not see." That tranquility, Ibn ‘Abbas said, came down on Abu Bakr, for the Prophet ﷺ had never been without it. And the forces no one saw, some explained, were angels turning the searchers' faces and eyes away from the cave.

paragraphs.text: The two were not cut off. Abu Bakr had given his son and his freedman their tasks. His son ‘Abdullah, a sharp young man who was quick to learn, spent each night with them in the cave and left in the last hours before dawn. By morning he was among Quraysh in Makkah, as if he had slept there. All day he listened to what they said and planned against the two, and kept every word of it in his head; when darkness closed in, he was back at the cave with the news.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr's freedman, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, grazed a flock of milking sheep among the shepherds of Makkah, where no one paid him any attention. Some time after nightfall he brought the flock to the cave, and the two slept with fresh milk; in the dark before dawn he called the sheep and drove them off again. When ‘Abdullah set out for Makkah in the morning, ‘Amir drove the flock along his trail, so that the sheep wiped out his footprints. Every evening, too, Asma brought them food. So it went, every one of the three nights.

paragraphs.text: At last the three nights passed, and the talk about the two died down. On the morning after the third night, the guide they had hired, ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, came to the cave as arranged, with their two camels and a third of his own. By the reckoning of later biographers, it was the night of Monday, the first of Rabi‘ al-Awwal.

In another telling, it was here at the cave, not at home, that her waistband served them: she had forgotten a strap to hang the bag by, and when the two were ready to leave there was nothing to tie it on. So she undid the waistband she wore, split it in two, hung the bag with one half and kept the other around her waist. From then on she was known as Dhat al-Nitaqayn, "she of the two waistbands", a name she carried all her life. The camels were ready, and the road to Madinah lay ahead.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr's words in the cave come from Abu Bakr himself, through Anas ibn Malik, and both al-Bukhari and Muslim record them. The tellings differ slightly. In Muslim, Abu Bakr saw "the feet of the idolaters above our heads" and feared one of them would look "at his feet"; the Prophet ﷺ answered, "Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?" In al-Bukhari, Abu Bakr raised his head, saw the men's feet and feared one of them would "lower his gaze"; the reply begins "Be quiet, Abu Bakr: two, and Allah is their third." Another chain in al-Bayhaqi has "if one of them raised his foot." The story above follows Muslim's wording. The calm that came down, and the words "Do not grieve", are from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr's account, which uses the words of the verse.

paragraphs.text: The verse says Allah "sent down His tranquility upon him." Ibn ‘Abbas held that this meant Abu Bakr, because the Prophet ﷺ had never been without it; others said it meant the Prophet ﷺ. For the "forces you did not see", al-Baghawi gives angels turning the searchers' faces and eyes away from him, or fear cast into their hearts until they went back.

paragraphs.text: The web over the entrance comes from a report of Ibn ‘Abbas recorded by Ahmad. Ibn Kathir called its chain hasan (good) and "among the best of what is reported about the spider's web over the mouth of the cave", and Ibn Hajar also called it hasan. The modern hadith scholar al-Albani disagreed: one narrator, ‘Uthman al-Jazari, is weak in his judgment. He also argued that the verse speaks of forces "you did not see", which a spider's web is not. That is why the story gives the web as Ibn ‘Abbas's report rather than as settled fact.

paragraphs.text: Other stories of the cave did not hold up. A longer report adds a tree that grew across the entrance and two wild pigeons nesting there; al-Albani judged it munkar (rejected), and Muhammad al-‘Awshan notes that no scholar he knew of authenticated the pigeons. A story of Abu Bakr blocking a hole with his foot and being stung by snakes was judged by al-Dhahabi to resemble the inventions of street storytellers.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr walking ahead of and behind the Prophet ﷺ, and asking him to wait while he checked the cave, come from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who reports what ‘Umar used to say: that one night of Abu Bakr's was better than the whole family of ‘Umar. Abu Bakr feeling his way around the cave for an animal or a snake comes from al-Hasan al-Basri, a report that reached Ibn Hisham from "some scholars" he does not name. Asma's encounter with Abu Jahl is also a single report: Ibn Ishaq says only that he "was told" it from Asma.

paragraphs.text: ‘Aishah's account in al-Bukhari, Ibn Ishaq, Mujahid and al-Zuhri all give three nights. In one version of ‘Urwah's account, recorded by al-Bayhaqi, the two stayed two days and two nights, while Musa ibn ‘Uqbah's version has three. Later biographers put dates to the stay. Al-Mubarakfuri, a modern biographer, names the nights of Friday, Saturday and Sunday, with the guide arriving on the night of Monday, the first of Rabi‘ al-Awwal. Al-Samhudi cites Ibn al-Kalbi for the same night of leaving the cave.

source_units.text_ar: فقد سلك الطريق الذي يضاده تماما، وهو الطريق الواقع جنوب مكة، والمتجه نحو اليمن. سلك هذا الطريق نحو خمسة أميال، حتى بلغ إلى جبل يعرف بجبل ثور
source_units.text: He took a route going in exactly the opposite direction: the road south of Makkah, leading toward Yemen. He followed this road for about five miles, until he reached a mountain known as Mount Thawr.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ: ثُمَّ لَحِقَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ بِغَارٍ فِي جَبَلِ ثَوْرٍ، فَكَمَنَا فِيهِ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ، يَبِيتُ عِنْدَهُمَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَهُوَ غُلَامٌ شَابٌّ، ثَقِفٌ لَقِنٌ، فَيُدْلِجُ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمَا بِسَحَرٍ، فَيُصْبِحُ مَعَ قُرَيْشٍ بِمَكَّةَ كَبَائِتٍ، فَلَا يَسْمَعُ أَمْرًا يُكْتَادَانِ بِهِ إِلَّا وَعَاهُ، حَتَّى يَأْتِيَهُمَا بِخَبَرِ ذَلِكَ حِينَ يَخْتَلِطُ الظَّلَامُ، وَيَرْعَى عَلَيْهِمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِنْحَةً مِنْ غَنَمٍ، فَيُرِيحُهَا عَلَيْهِمَا حِينَ تَذْهَبُ سَاعَةٌ مِنَ الْعِشَاءِ، فَيَبِيتَانِ فِي رِسْلٍ، وَهُوَ لَبَنُ مِنْحَتِهِمَا وَرَضِيفِهِمَا، حَتَّى يَنْعِقَ بِهَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ بِغَلَسٍ، يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ فِي كُلِّ لَيْلَةٍ مِنْ تِلْكَ اللَّيَالِي الثَّلَاثِ،
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr reached a cave on Mount Thawr and hid there for three nights. Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, an alert, quick-witted young man, spent the night with them. He would leave them in the last part of the night and be among Quraysh in Makkah in the morning as though he had slept there. Whenever he heard of a plot against the two of them, he retained it, until he brought them news of it when darkness mingled. Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, tended a milch flock of sheep for them and brought it back to them after some time of the night had passed. They spent the night with risl, that is, the milk of their milch flock, and their radif (الرضيف), until Amir ibn Fuhayrah called to the flock at the dark of dawn. He did this every night of those three nights,

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَأَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْغَارِ ثَلَاثًا وَمَعَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَجَعَلَتْ قُرَيْشٌ فِيهِ حِين فقدوه مائَة نَاقَةٍ، لِمَنْ يَرُدُّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained in the cave for three nights, with Abu Bakr. When Quraysh lost him, they offered a hundred camels to anyone who brought him back to them.

source_units.text_ar: «أَنَّهُمْ رَكِبُوا فِي كُلِّ وَجْهٍ يَطْلُبُونَ النَّبِيَّ ﵌ وَبَعَثُوا إِلَى أَهْلِ الْمِيَاهِ يَأْمُرُونَهُمْ وَيَجْعَلُونَ لَهُمُ الْجُعَلَ الْعَظِيمَ، وَأَتَوْا عَلَى ثَوْرِ الْجَبَلِ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْغَارُ الَّذِي فِيهِ النَّبِيُّ ﵌ حَتَّى طَلَعُوا فَوْقَهُ، وَسَمِعَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ أَصْوَاتَهُمْ، فَأَشْفَقَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْهَمُّ وَالْخَوْفُ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ يَقُولُ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌: لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا، وَدَعَا رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌، فَنَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِنَ اللهِ
source_units.speaker_ar: عروة في اللفظ الذي يعيّنه تعقيب البيهقي
source_units.text: “They rode out in every direction seeking the Prophet ﷺ and sent word to the people at the watering places, ordering them to help and promising them a great reward. They came to Mount Thawr, where the cave in which the Prophet ﷺ was staying lay, and climbed up until they reached its top. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr heard their voices. Abu Bakr became alarmed, and worry and fear overcame him. At that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘Do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, and tranquility from Allah descended upon him.”

source_units.text_ar: فَأَنْزَلَ اللهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
source_units.kind_ar: صياغة السكينة في خبر عروة لا آية مطابقة
source_units.speaker_ar: صياغة داخل خبر عروة كما نقلت؛ ليست مقابلة كاملة لآية التوبة
source_units.text: “Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers,”

source_units.text_ar: وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَى وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيا وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ [(٢٥)] .
source_units.kind_ar: خاتمة قرآنية منقولة ضمن الخبر لا آية كاملة
source_units.speaker_ar: القرآن كما ورد في خبر عروة
source_units.text: “and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is supreme. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَ: تَشَاوَرَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لَيْلَةً بِمَكَّةَ، فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: إِذَا أَصْبَحَ فَأَثْبِتُوهُ بِالْوَثَاقِ، يُرِيدُونَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ.
وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: بَلِ اقْتُلُوهُ.
وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: بَلْ أَخْرِجُوهُ.
فَأَطْلَعَ اللَّهُ نَبِيَّهُ ﷺ عَلَى ذَلِكَ، فَبَاتَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَى فِرَاشِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، وَخَرَجَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ حَتَّى لَحِقَ بِالْغَارِ، وَبَاتَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ يَحْرُسُونَ عَلِيًّا يَحْسَبُونَهُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ.
فَلَمَّا أَصْبحُوا ثَارُوا عَلَيْهِ، فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا عَلِيًّا رَدَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مَكْرَهُمْ.
فَقَالُوا: أَيْنَ صَاحِبُكَ هَذَا؟ فَقَالَ: لَا أَدْرِي.
فاقتفوا أَثَرَهُ، فَلَمَّا بَلَغُوا الْجَبَلَ اخْتَلَطَ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَصَعِدُوا الْجَبَلَ فَمَرُّوا بِالْغَارِ، فَرَأَوْا عَلَى بَابِهِ نَسْجَ العنكبوت، فَقَالُوا: لَو دخل هَا هُنَا أَحَدٌ لَمْ يَكُنْ نَسْجُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ عَلَى بَابِهِ، فَمَكَثَ فِيهِ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن عباس في نقل ابن كثير عن أحمد

He said: One night in Makkah, Quraysh deliberated. Some of them said, “When morning comes, bind him securely”—meaning the Prophet ﷺ. Others said, “Rather, kill him.” Still others said, “Rather, drive him out.”

Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of this. That night, ‘Ali lay in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed, while the Prophet ﷺ went out and reached the cave. The polytheists spent the night keeping watch over ‘Ali, thinking he was the Prophet ﷺ.

When morning came, they rushed at him. But when they saw ‘Ali, Allah thwarted their plot. They said, “Where is your companion?” He replied, “I do not know.”

They followed his trail. When they reached the mountain, they lost track of it. They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. Seeing a spider’s web across its entrance, they said, “If anyone had entered here, there would not be a spider’s web at its entrance.” He remained there for three nights.

source_units.text_ar: فصعدوا الجبل فمروا بالغار، فرأوا على بابه نسج العنكبوت، فقالوا: لو دخل ها هنا أحد لم يكن نسج العنكبوت على بابه، فمكث فيه ثلاث ليال. وهذا إسناد حسن، وهو من أجود ما روي في قصة نسج العنكبوت على فم الغار

source_units.text: They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. They saw a spider’s web at its entrance and said, “If anyone had gone in here, there would not be a spider’s web at its entrance.” He stayed there for three nights. This is a sound chain of transmission, and it is among the best reports narrated about the spider’s web at the mouth of the cave.

source_units.text_ar:
حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَبْدِ اللهِ الْحَافِظُ إِمْلَاءً، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرٍ: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَفَّانُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا السَّرِيُّ بْنُ يَحْيَى، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِيرِينَ، قَالَ:
«ذُكِرَ رِجَالٌ عَلَى عَهْدِ عُمَرَ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ فَضَلُّوا عُمَرَ عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄، فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ ذَلِكَ عُمَرُ ﵁، قَالَ: وَاللهِ لَلَيْلَةٌ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ آلِ عُمَرَ، وَلَيَوْمٌ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ آلِ عُمَرَ، لَقَدْ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ لَيْلَةَ انْطَلَقَ إِلَى الْغَارِ وَمَعَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁، فَجَعَلَ يَمْشِي سَاعَةً بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَسَاعَةً خَلْفَهُ، حَتَّى فَطِنَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌، فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ مَالِكَ تَمْشِي سَاعَةً بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ وَسَاعَةً خَلْفِي؟ فَقَالَ. يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ أَذْكُرُ الطَّلَبَ، فَأَمْشِي خَلْفَكَ، ثُمَّ أَذْكُرُ الرَّصَدَ فَأَمْشِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ، فَقَالَ: يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ لَوْ كَانَ شَيْءٌ أَحْبَبْتَ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَكَ دُونِي؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ، وَالَّذِي بَعَثَكَ بِالْحَقِّ مَا كَانَتْ لِتَكُنْ مِنْ مُلِمَّةٍ إِلَّا أَحْبَبْتُ أَنْ تَكُونَ لِي دُونَكَ،
فَلَمَّا انْتَهَيْنَا مِنَ الْغَارِ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁: مَكَانَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ حَتَّى استبري لَكَ الْغَارَ فَدَخَلَ فَاسْتَبْرَأَهُ حَتَّى إِذَا كَانَ فِي أَعْلَاهُ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَسْتَبْرِ الْجُحْرَةَ، فَقَالَ: مَكَانَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ حَتَّى استبري الْجُحْرَةَ، فَدَخَلَ فَاسْتَبْرَأَ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: انْزِلْ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، فَنَزَلَ فَقَالَ عُمَرُ: وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ لَتِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةُ خَيْرٌ مِنْ آلِ عُمَرَ.
source_units.speaker_ar: محمد بن سيرين ينقل قول عمر
source_units.text:
Abu ‘Abdullah al-Hafiz dictated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn al-Hasan ibn ‘Abbad informed us, saying: ‘Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: al-Sari ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, saying:
“Some men were mentioned during ‘Umar’s time, and it seemed they were giving ‘Umar precedence over Abu Bakr. When ‘Umar heard of this, he said, ‘By Allah, one night of Abu Bakr’s is better than all of ‘Umar’s family, and one day of Abu Bakr’s is better than all of ‘Umar’s family. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out one night for the cave, accompanied by Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr would walk for a while ahead of him and then for a while behind him, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed. He said, “Abu Bakr, why do you walk for a while ahead of me and then for a while behind me?” He replied, “Messenger of Allah, I think of the pursuers, so I walk behind you; then I think of those lying in wait, so I walk ahead of you.” He said, “Abu Bakr, if something were to happen, would you want it to happen to you rather than to me?” He replied, “Yes. By the One who sent you with the truth, whenever calamity threatened, I would want it to befall me and not you.”
“When we reached the cave, Abu Bakr said, ‘Stay here, Messenger of Allah, until I inspect the cave for you.’ He went in and inspected it. When he reached the upper part, he remembered that he had not checked the hole. He said, ‘Stay here, Messenger of Allah, until I inspect the hole.’ He went in and checked it, then said, ‘Come down, Messenger of Allah.’ He came down, and ‘Umar said, ‘By the One in whose hand is my soul, that night is better than all of ‘Umar’s family.’”

source_units.text_ar: ﴿إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ﴾
source_units.speaker_ar: الآية كما يقتبسها البغوي
source_units.text: “When the two of them were in the cave”

source_units.text_ar: وَهُوَ نَقْبٌ فِي جَبَلِ ثَوْرٍ بِمَكَّةَ،
source_units.speaker_ar: البغوي
source_units.text: It is a crevice in Mount Thawr in Makkah.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَحَدَّثَنِي بَعْضُ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ، أَنَّ الْحَسَنَ بْنَ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيَّ قَالَ: انْتَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ إلَى الْغَارِ لَيْلًا، فَدَخَلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁ قَبْلَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَلَمَسَ الْغَارَ، لِيَنْظُرَ أَفِيهِ سَبُعٌ أَوْ حَيَّةٌ، يَقِي رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِنَفْسِهِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن هشام ينقل عن بعض أهل العلم عن الحسن البصري
source_units.text: Ibn Hisham said: Some people of knowledge told me that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr reached the cave at night. Abu Bakr went in before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and felt around inside the cave to see whether there was a wild animal or a snake, protecting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his own life.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَحُدِّثْتُ عَنْ أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ: لَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁، أَتَانَا نَفَرٌ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، فِيهِمْ أَبُو جَهْلِ ابْن هِشَامٍ، فَوَقَفُوا عَلَى بَابِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، فَخَرَجْتُ إلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالُوا: أَيْنَ أَبُوكَ يَا بِنْتَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ؟ قَالَتْ: قُلْتُ: لَا أَدْرِي وَاَللَّهِ أَيْنَ أَبِي؟ قَالَتْ: فَرَفَعَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ يَدَهُ، وَكَانَ فَاحِشًا خَبِيثًا، فَلَطَمَ خَدِّي لَطْمَةً طُرِحَ مِنْهَا قُرْطِي.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق ينقل عن أسماء بصيغة فحدثت
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: I was told by Asma’ bint Abu Bakr that she said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr left, a group of Quraysh came to us, among them Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. They stopped at Abu Bakr’s door, and I went out to them. They said, “Where is your father, daughter of Abu Bakr?” I said, “By Allah, I don’t know where my father is.” She said: Abu Jahl raised his hand—he was vile and wicked—and slapped me so hard that my earring fell off.

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَحَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ عَبَّادًا حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ جَدَّتِهِ أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، قَالَتْ: لَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَخَرَجَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مَعَهُ، احْتَمَلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مَالَهُ كُلَّهُ، وَمَعَهُ خَمْسَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ أَوْ سِتَّةُ آلَافٍ، فَانْطَلَقَ بِهَا مَعَهُ. قَالَتْ: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا جَدِّي أَبُو قُحَافَةَ، وَقَدْ ذَهَبَ بَصَرُهُ، فَقَالَ: وَاَللَّهِ إنِّي لَا أَرَاهُ قَدْ فَجَعَكُمْ بِمَالِهِ مَعَ نَفْسِهِ. قَالَتْ: قُلْتُ:
كَلَّا يَا أَبَتِ! إنَّهُ قَدْ تَرَكَ لَنَا خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا. قَالَتْ: فَأَخَذْتُ أَحْجَارًا فَوَضَعْتهَا فِي كُوَّةٍ فِي الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي كَانَ أَبِي يَضَعُ مَالَهُ فِيهَا، ثُمَّ وَضَعْتُ عَلَيْهَا ثَوْبًا، ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ بِيَدِهِ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا أَبَتِ، ضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى هَذَا الْمَالِ. قَالَتْ: فَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:
لَا بَأْسَ، إذَا كَانَ تَرَكَ لَكُمْ هَذَا فَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ، وَفِي هَذَا بَلَاغٌ لَكُمْ. وَلَا وَاَللَّهِ مَا تَرَكَ لَنَا شَيْئًا وَلَكِنِّي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُسَكِّنَ الشَّيْخَ بِذَلِكَ.
source_units.speaker_ar: أسماء في رواية ابن إسحاق

source_units.text_ar: ٣٩٢٢ - حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ: حَدَّثَنَا هَمَّامٌ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵁ قَالَ:
source_units.kind_ar: إسناد داخل الانتقاء مع وسم رقمي
source_units.speaker_ar: أنس عن أبي بكر
source_units.text: ٣٩٢٢ - Musa ibn Ismail related to us: Hammam related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from Abu Bakr ﵁, who said:

source_units.text_ar: <hadeeth-1622>«كُنْتُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي الْغَارِ؟ فَرَفَعْتُ رَأْسِي فَإِذَا أَنَا بِأَقْدَامِ الْقَوْمِ؟ فَقُلْتُ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللهِ؟ لَوْ أَنَّ بَعْضَهُمْ طَأْطَأَ بَصَرَهُ رَآنَا، قَالَ: اسْكُتْ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، اثْنَانِ اللهُ ثَالِثُهُمَا.»
source_units.speaker_ar: أنس عن أبي بكر
source_units.text: “I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave? I raised my head and there were the men’s feet? I said: O Prophet of Allah? If one of them lowered his gaze, he would see us. He said: Be quiet, Abu Bakr; two, with Allah as their third.”

source_units.text_ar:
١ - (٢٣٨١) حَدَّثَنِي زُهَيْرُ بْنُ حَرْبٍ وَعَبْدُ بْنُ حميد وعبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الدارمي (قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: أَخْبَرَنَا. وقَالَ الْآخَرَانِ: حَدَّثَنَا)
حَبَّانُ بْنُ هِلَالٍ. حَدَّثَنَا هَمَّامٌ. حَدَّثَنَا ثَابِتٌ. حَدَّثَنَا أَنَسُ بْنُ مَالِكٍ؛
أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقَ حَدَّثَهُ قَالَ:
source_units.speaker_ar: المصنف في سلسلة النقل، لا شاهد حاضر جديد
source_units.text: ١ - (٢٣٨١) Zuhayr ibn Harb, Abd ibn Humayd, and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi related to me (Abd Allah said: He informed us; the other two said: He related to us). Habban ibn Hilal related to us. Hammam related to us. Thabit related to us. Anas ibn Malik related to us that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq related to him, saying:

source_units.text_ar: نَظَرْتُ إِلَى أَقْدَامِ المشركين على رؤوسنا وَنَحْنُ فِي الْغَارِ. فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ! لَوْ أَنَّ أَحَدَهُمْ نَظَرَ إِلَى قَدَمَيْهِ أَبْصَرَنَا تَحْتَ قَدَمَيْهِ. فَقَالَ "يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ! مَا ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما".
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية أنس؛ ليس أنس شاهد الغار في هذا النص
source_units.text: I looked at the feet of the polytheists above our heads while we were in the cave. I said: O Messenger of Allah! If one of them looked at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet. He said: “Abu Bakr! What do you think of two whose third is Allah?”

source_units.text_ar: وخرج المشركون يطلبونهما حتى جاءوا إلى الجبل وأشرفوا على الغار،
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو حاتم ابن حبان في سرده؛ المتكلم الداخلي كما في النص
source_units.book_ar: السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان
source_units.citation_ar: [السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان، 1/129](https://app.turath.io/book/9898?page=124)
source_units.text: The polytheists set out in pursuit of the two of them. They came to the mountain and looked down toward the cave.

source_units.text_ar: فقال أبو بكر: يا رسول الله! لو أبصر أحدهم تحت قدمه «٥» لأبصرنا «٦»، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «يا أبا بكر! ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما»،
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو حاتم ابن حبان في سرده؛ المتكلم الداخلي كما في النص
source_units.book_ar: السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان
source_units.citation_ar: [السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان، 1/129](https://app.turath.io/book/9898?page=124)
source_units.text: Abu Bakr said, “Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to look beneath his feet, he would see us.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is the third of them?”

source_units.text_ar: فأعمى الله «٧» أعينهم عن رسول الله ﷺ، فلما أيسوا رجعوا،
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو حاتم ابن حبان في سرده؛ المتكلم الداخلي كما في النص
source_units.book_ar: السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان
source_units.citation_ar: [السيرة النبوية وأخبار الخلفاء من الثقات لابن حبان، 1/129](https://app.turath.io/book/9898?page=124)
source_units.text: Allah blinded their eyes to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they had given up hope, they turned back.

source_units.text_ar: إِلاَّ تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُما فِي الْغارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنا فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْها وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلى وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيا وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ (٤٠)
source_units.speaker_ar: نص الآية في تفسير القرطبي
source_units.text: If you do not help him, Allah has already helped him, when those who disbelieved drove him out as one of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.” Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him, supported him with forces you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. Allah is mighty, wise. (٤٠)

source_units.text_ar: فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّه سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ
source_units.kind_ar: قرآن منقول في المصدر؛ لا مقابلة مستقلة للمصحف
source_units.speaker_ar: مقتطف الآية في خبر ابن عباس
source_units.text: “So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ: عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ لِأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﵌ لَمْ تَزَلِ السَّكِينَةُ معه» .
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن عباس كما يسند البيهقي، لا قول تحريري
source_units.text: He said: “Upon Abu Bakr, because tranquility had never ceased to be with the Prophet ﷺ.”

source_units.text_ar: ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ﴾
source_units.kind_ar: قرآن منقول في المصدر؛ لا مقابلة مستقلة للمصحف
source_units.speaker_ar: مقتطف الآية كما أورده المفسر
source_units.text: “So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him.”

source_units.text_ar: قِيلَ: عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ. وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: عَلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵁، فَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ السَّكِينَةُ مِنْ قَبْلُ،
source_units.speaker_ar: البغوي ينقل القولين في الضمير
source_units.text: It was said: Upon the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn ‘Abbas said: Upon Abu Bakr, for the Prophet ﷺ had already been granted tranquility before that.

source_units.text_ar: ﴿وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾
source_units.kind_ar: قرآن منقول في المصدر؛ لا مقابلة مستقلة للمصحف
source_units.speaker_ar: مقتطف الآية كما أورده المفسر
source_units.text: “And He strengthened him with forces you did not see.”

source_units.speaker_ar: البغوي ينقل القولين في الضمير

source_units.text_ar: وَهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ نَزَلُوا يَصْرِفُونَ وَجُوهَ الْكَفَّارِ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ عَنْ رُؤْيَتِهِ. وَقِيلَ: أَلْقَوُا الرُّعْبَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْكُفَّارِ حَتَّى رَجَعُوا.
source_units.speaker_ar: البغوي في عرض الأقوال في الجنود
source_units.text: They were the angels. They descended, turning the faces and eyes of the disbelievers away from seeing him. It was also said: They cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers until they turned back.

source_units.text_ar: وَأَمَرَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ابْنَهُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ أَنْ يَتَسَمَّعَ لَهُمَا مَا يَقُولُ النَّاسُ فِيهِمَا نَهَارَهُ، ثُمَّ يَأْتِيهِمَا إذَا أَمْسَى بِمَا يَكُونُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ مِنْ الْخَبَرِ،
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: Abu Bakr instructed his son, ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, to listen during the day to what people were saying about the two of them, then to come to them at dusk with whatever news there was that day.

source_units.text_ar: وَأَمَرَ عَامِرَ بْنَ فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَاهُ أَنْ يَرْعَى غَنَمَهُ نَهَارَهُ، ثُمَّ يُرِيحُهَا عَلَيْهِمَا، يَأْتِيهِمَا إذَا أَمْسَى فِي الْغَارِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: He instructed his freedman, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, to graze his sheep during the day, then bring them to rest with the two of them, coming to them at dusk in the cave.

source_units.text_ar: وَكَانَتْ أَسَمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ تَأْتِيهِمَا مِنْ الطَّعَامِ إذَا أَمْسَتْ بِمَا يُصْلِحُهُمَا.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: When evening came, Asma’ bint Abi Bakr would bring them whatever food they needed.

source_units.text_ar: وَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ يَكُونُ فِي قُرَيْشٍ نَهَارَهُ مَعَهُمْ، يَسْمَعُ مَا يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِهِ، وَمَا يَقُولُونَ فِي شَأْنِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَأَبِي بَكْرٍ، ثُمَّ يَأْتِيهِمَا إذَا أَمْسَى فَيُخْبِرُهُمَا الْخَبَرَ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: During the day, ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr would be among Quraysh, listening to what they planned and what they said about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr. Then, when evening came, he would go to them and tell them the news.

source_units.text_ar: وَكَانَ عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ، مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵁، يَرْعَى فِي رَعْيَانِ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ، فَإِذَا أَمْسَى أَرَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا غَنَمَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، فَاحْتَلَبَا وَذَبَحَا، فَإِذَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ غَدَا مِنْ عِنْدِهِمَا إلَى مَكَّةَ، اتَّبَعَ عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ أَثَرَهُ بِالْغَنَمِ حَتَّى يُعَفِّي عَلَيْهِ،
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freedman, would graze among the shepherds of the people of Makkah. When evening came, he would bring Abu Bakr’s sheep to them. They would milk them and slaughter one. When ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr set out from them for Makkah in the morning, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah would follow his tracks with the sheep until he erased them.

source_units.text_ar: حَتَّى إذَا مَضَتْ الثَّلَاثُ، وَسَكَنَ عَنْهُمَا النَّاسُ أَتَاهُمَا صَاحِبُهُمَا الَّذِي اسْتَأْجَرَاهُ بِبَعِيرَيْهِمَا وَبَعِيرٍ لَهُ، وَأَتَتْهُمَا أَسَمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄ بِسُفْرَتِهِمَا، وَنَسِيَتْ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ لَهَا عِصَامًا فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَا ذَهَبَتْ لِتُعَلِّقَ السُّفْرَةَ، فَإِذَا لَيْسَ لَهَا عِصَامٌ، [١] فَتَحِلُّ نِطَاقَهَا فَتَجْعَلُهُ عِصَامًا، ثُمَّ عَلَّقَتْهَا بِهِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق
source_units.text: When the three days had passed and the people had ceased searching for them, the man they had hired came to them with their two camels and a camel of his own. Asma’ bint Abi Bakr brought them their provisions, but she had forgotten to bring a cord for tying them. When they set out, she went to fasten the provisions, but found she had no cord. So she untied her waist belt, used it as a cord, and tied the provisions with it.

source_units.text_ar: يَكُونُ فِي مَكَّةَ وَيَرُوحُ عَلَيْهِمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ الْغَنَمَ كُلَّ لَيْلَةٍ فَيَحْلِبَانِ وَيُدْلِجَانِ ثُمَّ يَسْرَحُ بُكْرَةً فَيُصْبِحُ فِي رُعْيَانِ النَّاسِ فَلَا يُفْطَنُ لَهُ حَتَّى إِذَا هَدَأَتْ عَنْهُمَا الْأَصْوَاتُ وَأَتَاهُمَا إِنْ قَدْ سُكِتَ عَنْهُمَا جَاءَ صَاحِبُهُمَا بِبَعِيرَيْهِمَا وَقَدْ مَكَثَا فِي الْغَارِ يَوْمَيْنِ وَلَيْلَتَيْنِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: عروة في اللفظ الذي يعينه البيهقي في تعقيبه
source_units.text: He would stay in Makkah, and every night ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah would bring the sheep to them. They would milk them and set out in the latter part of the night. Then, in the morning, he would take the sheep out to pasture and be among the people’s shepherds, so no one would notice him. When the voices had quieted around them and it was known that they were no longer being pursued, their companion came to them with their two camels. They had remained in the cave for two days and two nights.

source_units.text_ar: وَفِي رِوَايَةِ مُوسَى بْنِ عُقْبَةَ- ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ
source_units.kind_ar: عبارة المدة المعينة لرواية موسى بن عقبة
source_units.speaker_ar: تعيين الناقل مدة رواية موسى بثلاث ليال؛ لا تعميم ذلك على لفظ كل التتمة
source_units.text: In the narration of Musa ibn ‘Uqbah: three nights.

source_units.text_ar: وَاسْتَأْجَرَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي الدِّيلِ، وَهُوَ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ بْنِ عَدِيٍّ، هَادِيًا خِرِّيتًا، وَالْخِرِّيتُ الْمَاهِرُ بِالْهِدَايَةِ، قَدْ غَمَسَ حِلْفًا فِي آلِ الْعَاصِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ السَّهْمِيِّ، وَهُوَ عَلَى دِينِ كُفَّارِ قُرَيْشٍ، فَأَمِنَاهُ فَدَفَعَا إِلَيْهِ رَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا، وَوَاعَدَاهُ
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dil, who belonged to Banu Abd ibn Adi, as a khirrit guide—that is, one skilled at finding the way. He had entered into an alliance with the family of al-As ibn Wail al-Sahmi, and he followed the faith of Quraysh’s unbelievers. They trusted him, handed over their two riding camels to him, and made an appointment with him at

source_units.text_ar: غَارَ ثَوْرٍ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ، بِرَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا صُبْحَ ثَلَاثٍ، وَانْطَلَقَ مَعَهُمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ، وَالدَّلِيلُ، فَأَخَذَ بِهِمْ طَرِيقَ السَّوَاحِلِ.»
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في الحديث نفسه
source_units.text: the Cave of Thawr after three nights, to bring their two riding camels on the morning of the third. Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the guide set out with them, and the guide took them along the coastal route.”

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: قَالَتْ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا قَوْلَهُ، عَرَفْنَا حَيْثُ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَنَّ وَجْهَهُ إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانُوا أَرْبَعَةً: رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵁، وَعَامِرُ ابْن فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَرْقَطَ دَلِيلُهُمَا.
قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَيُقَالُ: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُرَيْقِطٍ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق ثم ابن هشام
source_units.text:
Ibn Ishaq said: Asma’ bint Abi Bakr said: “When we heard what he said, we knew where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was headed, and that he was headed for Madinah. There were four of them: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Abu Bakr’s freedman ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and their guide, ‘Abdullah ibn Arqat.”
Ibn Hisham said: It is also said that he was ‘Abdullah ibn Uraiqit.

source_units.text_ar: رجع الحديث إلى الأوّل، قالوا: وكانت لأبي بكر منيحة غنم يرعاها عامر بن فُهَيرة، وكان يأتيهم بها ليلًا فيحتلبون فإذا كان سَحَرٌ سرح مع الناس.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر
source_units.text: The account returns to the beginning. They said: Abu Bakr had a flock of sheep given to him as a gift, which ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah tended. He would bring them to them at night, and they would milk them. At daybreak, he would take them out to graze with the people.

source_units.text_ar: قالت عائشة: وجهّزناهما أحبّ الجهاز، وصنعنا لهما سُفْرة في جِراب فقطعت أسماء بنت أبي بكر قطعة من نطاقها فَأوْكَت به الجراب، وقَطَعت أُخرى فصيّرته عِصامًا لفم القِرْبة، فبذلك سُمِّيَت ذات النطاقين.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر
source_units.text: ‘Aishah said: “We prepared provisions for the two of them as well as we could, and packed food for them in a leather bag. Asma’ bint Abu Bakr cut a strip from her waistband and tied the bag with it. She cut another strip and made it a tie for the mouth of the waterskin. For this reason she was called ‘the woman of the two waistbands.’”

source_units.text_ar: ومكثَ رسول الله، - ﷺ -، وأبو بكر في الغار ثلاث ليال، يبيت عندهما عبد الله بن أبي بكر، واستأجر أبو بكر رجلًا من بني الدِّيل هاديًا خِرِّيتًا (^١) يقال له عبد الله بن أرَيْقط، وهو على دين الكفر. ولكنّهما أمناه، فارتحلا ومعهما عامر بن فُهيرة، فأخذ بهم ابن أريقط يَدَ بَحْرٍ (^٢)، فما شعرت قريش أين وَجّه رسول الله، - ﷺ -.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر
source_units.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr stayed in the cave for three nights. ‘Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr would spend the night with them. Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl, a skilled guide, named ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, who followed the religion of unbelief. But the two of them trusted him. They set out, accompanied by ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, and Ibn Urayqit led them along a coastal route. Quraysh had no idea where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone.

source_units.text_ar:
حتى سمعوا صوتًا من جنّيّ من أسفل مكّة، ولا يُرى شخصُه:
جَزَى اللهُ رب النّاس خيرَ جَزَائِهِ … رَفيقينِ قالا خَيْمَتَيْ أمّ مَعْبدِ
هُمَا نَزَلا بالبِرّ وَارْتَحَلا بِهِ … فقد فازَ مَنْ أمْسى رَفيقَ محَمّد
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر
source_units.text:
Until they heard the voice of a jinn from below Makkah, though he could not be seen:
“May Allah, Lord of the people, reward with the best reward … two companions who stayed at the tent of Umm Ma‘bad.
They came down with goodness and departed with it … whoever spends the evening as Muhammad’s companion has indeed prospered.”

source_units.text_ar: وكمنا في الغار ثلاث ليال، ليلة الجمعة وليلة السبت وليلة الأحد
source_units.text: They remained in the cave for three nights: Friday night, Saturday night, and Sunday night.

source_units.text_ar: فلما كانت ليلة الإثنين- غرة ربيع الأول سنة ١ ه/ ١٦ سبتمبر سنة ٦٢٢ م- جاءهما عبد الله بن أريقط بالراحلتين
source_units.text: When Monday night came—the first of Rabi‘ al-Awwal in the year 1 AH, September 16, 622 CE—‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit came to them with the two riding camels.

source_units.text_ar:
فَكَانَ يُقَالُ لِأَسْمَاءِ بِنْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ: ذَاتُ النِّطَاقِ، لِذَلِكَ.
قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُ: ذَاتُ النِّطَاقَيْنِ.
وَتَفْسِيرُهُ: أَنَّهَا لَمَّا أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تُعَلِّقَ السُّفْرَةَ شَقَّتْ نِطَاقَهَا بِاثْنَيْنِ، فَعَلَّقَتْ السُّفْرَةَ بِوَاحِدٍ، وَانْتَطَقَتْ بِالْآخَرِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق ثم ابن هشام؛ عبارة قال ابن هشام تفصل التعليق
source_units.text: For this reason, Asma’ bint Abu Bakr used to be called “the woman with the waist-band.” Ibn Hisham said: I heard more than one scholar say “the woman with the two waist-bands.” The explanation is that when she wanted to tie up the travel provisions, she tore her waist-band in two, tied up the provisions with one piece, and wore the other as a waist-band.

source_units.text_ar:
وَأَخْبَرَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ عَبْدَانَ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ الصَّفَّارُ قَالَ:
حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ الْقُرَشِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا حَبَّانُ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا هَمَّامٌ عَنِ الْبُنَانِيِّ فَذَكَرَهُ بِإِسْنَادِهِ نَحْوَهُ إِلَّا أَنَّهُ قَالَ
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية أنس؛ والبيهقي في التخريج
source_units.text: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdan also informed us; he said: Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Saffar informed us; he said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muawiyah al-Qurashi related to us; he said: Habban related to us; he said: Hammam related to us from al-Bunani. He then related it with its chain in similar terms, except that he said:

source_units.text_ar: «لَوْ أَنَّ أَحَدَهُمْ رَفَعَ قَدَمَهُ لَأَبْصَرَنَا مِنْ تَحْتِ قَدَمَيْهِ» .
source_units.speaker_ar: أبو بكر برواية أنس؛ والبيهقي في التخريج
source_units.text: “If one of them raised his foot, he would see us from beneath his foot.”

source_units.text_ar:
رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي الصَّحِيحِ [(٣٠)] عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُفْيَانَ، وَعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّه بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ حَبَّانَ بْنِ هِلَالٍ.
وَرَوَاهُ مُسْلِمٌ عَنْ: زُهَيْرِ بْنِ حَرْبٍ [(٣١)]، وَغَيْرِهِ، عَنْ حَبَّانَ.
source_units.speaker_ar: البيهقي في التخريج؛ لا كلام أبي بكر
source_units.text: Al-Bukhari transmitted it in the Sahih [(٣٠)] from Muhammad ibn Sufyan, and from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Habban ibn Hilal. Muslim transmitted it from Zuhayr ibn Harb [(٣١)] and others, from Habban.

source_units.text_ar: وَهَذَا إِسْنَادٌ حَسَنٌ، وَهُوَ مِنْ أَجْوَدِ مَا رُوِيَ فِي قِصَّةِ نَسْجِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ عَلَى فَمِ الْغَارِ، وَذَلِكَ مِنْ حماية الله وَرَسُوله ﷺ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن كثير
source_units.book_ar: السيرة النبوية من البداية والنهاية - ت عبد الواحد
source_units.citation_ar: [السيرة النبوية من البداية والنهاية - ت عبد الواحد، 2/239](https://app.turath.io/book/930?page=761)
source_units.text: This is a good chain of transmission, and it is among the best reports narrated about the spider weaving its web at the mouth of the cave. This was part of Allah’s protection of His Messenger ﷺ.

source_units.text_ar: وَذَكَرَ أَحْمَدُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ بِإِسْنَادٍ حَسَنٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ .. الْآيَةَ، قَالَ: تَشَاوَرَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لَيْلَةً بِمَكَّةَ، فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: إِذَا أَصْبَحَ فَأَثْبِتُوهُ بِالْوَثَاقِ. يُرِيدُونَ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ. وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: بَلِ اقْتُلُوهُ. وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ: بَلْ أَخْرِجُوهُ. فَأَطْلَعَ اللَّهُ نَبِيَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَبَاتَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَى فِرَاشِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ، وَخَرَجَ - النَّبِيُّ ﷺ حَتَّى لَحِقَ بِالْغَارِ، وَبَاتَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ يَحْرُسُونَ عَلِيًّا يَحْسِبُونَهُ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ، يَعْنِي يَنْتَظِرُونَهُ حَتَّى يَقُومُ فَيَفْعَلُونَ بِهِ مَا اتَّفَقُوا عَلَيْهِ، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحُوا وَرَأَوْا عَلِيًّا رَدَّ اللَّهُ مَكْرَهُمْ فَقَالُوا: أَيْنَ صَاحِبُكَ هَذَا؟ قَالَ: لَا أَدْرِي. فَاقْتَصُّوا أَثَرَهُ، فَلِمَا بَلَغُوا الْجَبَلَ اخْتَلَطَ عَلَيْهِمْ، فَصَعِدُوا الْجَبَلَ فَمَرُّوا بِالْغَارِ فَرَأَوْا عَلَى بَابِهِ نَسْجَ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ فَقَالُوا: لَوْ دَخَلَ هَاهُنَا لَمْ يَكُنْ نَسْجُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ عَلَى بَابِهِ، فَمَكَثَ فِيهِ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ.

source_units.text: Ahmad related, with a good chain of transmission, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning the words of the Exalted: “And when those who disbelieved plotted against you”—to the end of the verse. He said: Quraysh consulted one another one night in Makkah. Some of them said, “When morning comes, bind him securely”—meaning the Prophet ﷺ. Others said, “Rather, kill him.” Others said, “Rather, drive him out.” Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of this, and that night ‘Ali slept in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed, while the Prophet ﷺ left and reached the cave. The polytheists spent the night keeping watch over ‘Ali, thinking he was the Prophet ﷺ—that is, waiting for him to get up so they could do to him what they had agreed upon. When morning came and they saw ‘Ali, Allah thwarted their plot. They said, “Where is your companion?” He replied, “I don’t know.” They followed his tracks, but when they reached the mountain they lost the trail. They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. They saw a spider’s web across its entrance and said, “Had he gone in here, there would not be a spider’s web across its entrance.” He remained there for three nights.

source_units.text_ar:
" تشاورت قريش ليلة بمكة، فقال بعضهم: إذا أصبح فأثبتوه بالوثاق يريدون النبي ﷺ، وقال بعضهم: اقتلوه، وقال بعضهم: بل أخرجوه، فأطلع الله ﷿ نبيه على ذلك، فبات علي على فراش النبي ﷺ تلك الليلة، وخرج النبي ﷺ حتى لحق بالغار، وبات المشركون يحرسون عليا، يحسبونه النبي ﷺ فلما أصبحوا ثاروا إليه، فلما رأوا عليا رد الله مكرهم، فقالوا: أين صاحبك هذا؟ قال: لا أدري، فاقتصوا أثره، فلما بلغوا الجبل خلط عليهم، فصعدوا في الجبل، فمروا بالغار، فرأوا
على بابه نسج العنكبوت، فقالوا: لودخل ههنا لم يكن نسج العنكبوت على بابه، فمكث فيه ثلاث ليال ".
قال ابن كثير عقبه:
" وهذا إسناد حسن، وهو من أجود ما روي في قصة العنكبوت على فم الغار ".
كذا قال، وليس بحسن في نقدي، لأن عثمان الجزري إن كان هو عثمان بن عمرو بن ساج الجزري فقد قال ابن أبي حاتم في " الجروح والتعديل " (٣/١/١٦٢) عن أبيه:
" لا يحتج به ".
وأورده الذهبي في " الضعفاء " وقال:
" تكلم فيه ".
وإن كان هو عثمان بن ساج الجزري ليس بينهما عمرو، فقد جنح الحافظ في " التهذيب " إلى أنه غير الأول، ولا يعرف حاله، ولم يفرق بينهما في " التقريب "، وقال:
" فيه ضعف ".
وابن عمرو لم يوثقه أحد غير ابن حبان، ومن المعروف تساهله في التوثيق، ولذلك فهو ضعيف لا يحتج به كما قال أبو حاتم.
وقال الهيثمي في " المجمع " (٧/٢٧):
" رواه أحمد والطبراني، وفيه عثمان بن عمرو الجزري، وثقه ابن حبان وضعفه غيره، وبقية رجاله رجال الصحيح ".
ولذلك قال المحقق أحمد شاكر في تعليقه على " المسند ":
" في إسناده نظر ".

“Quraysh consulted one another one night in Makkah. Some of them said, ‘When morning comes, bind him securely,’ meaning the Prophet ﷺ. Others said, ‘Kill him,’ and others said, ‘Rather, drive him out.’ Allah, Mighty and Exalted, informed His Prophet ﷺ of this. That night ‘Ali slept in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed, and the Prophet ﷺ left and reached the cave. The polytheists spent the night keeping watch over ‘Ali, thinking he was the Prophet ﷺ. When morning came, they rushed toward him. When they saw ‘Ali, Allah thwarted their plot. They said, ‘Where is your companion?’ He replied, ‘I don’t know.’ They followed his tracks, but when they reached the mountain they lost the trail. They climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. They saw a spider’s web across its entrance and said, ‘Had he gone in here, there would not be a spider’s web across its entrance.’ He remained there for three nights.”

Ibn Kathir said after it:

“This is a good chain of transmission, and it is among the best reports about the spider’s web at the mouth of the cave.”

That is what he said, but in my assessment it is not good. If ‘Uthman al-Jazari is ‘Uthman ibn ‘Amr ibn Saj al-Jazari, Abu Hatim said of him in al-Jarh wa al-Ta‘dil (3/1/162): “He is not authoritative.” Al-Dhahabi included him in al-Du‘afa’ and said: “He was criticized.” If he is ‘Uthman ibn Saj al-Jazari, without ‘Amr in his name, then the hadith scholar Ibn Hajar leaned in al-Tahdhib toward the view that he is not the former narrator, and his reliability is unknown. He did not distinguish between them in al-Taqrib, where he said: “He is weak.” No one declared Ibn ‘Amr reliable except Ibn Hibban, who is known to be lenient in declaring narrators reliable. Therefore, he is weak and not authoritative, as Abu Hatim said.

Al-Haythami said in Majma‘ al-Zawa’id (7/27): “Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it. It includes ‘Uthman ibn ‘Amr al-Jazari, whom Ibn Hibban declared reliable but others considered weak; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih collections.”

For this reason, the editor Ahmad Shakir said in his commentary on al-Musnad: “There is a problem with its chain of transmission.”

ثم إن الآية المتقدمة " وأيده بجنود لم تروها " فيها ما يؤكد ضعف الحديث، لأنها صريحة بأن النصر والتأييد إنما كان بجنود لا ترى، والحديث يثبت أن نصره ﷺ كان بالعنكبوت، وهو مما يرى، فتأمل.
والأشبه بالآية أن الجنود فيها إنما هم الملائكة، وليس العنكبوت ولا الحمامتين، ولذلك قال البغوي في " تفسيره " (٤/١٧٤) للآية:
" وهم الملائكة نزلوا يصرفون وجوه الكفار وأبصارهم عن رؤيته ".
وقد جاء في بعض الحديث ما يشهد لهذا المعنى، وهو ما أخرج أبو نعيم عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر ﵂:
" أن أبا بكر ﵁ رأى رجلا مواجه الغار، فقال: يا رسول الله إنه لرائينا، قال: كلا إن الملائكة تستره الآن بأجنحتها، فلم ينشب الرجل أن قعد يبول مستقبلهما، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: يا أبا بكر لوكان يراك ما فعل هذا ".
وأخرجه الطبراني مطولا في قصة الهجرة، وقال الهيثمي (٦/٥٤):
" رواه الطبراني وفيه يعقوب هذا أنه حسن الحديث، وقال الحافظ فيه:
" صدوق، ربما وهم ".
فإذا لم يكن في الإسناد علة أخرى فهو حسن، ولكني لا أستطيع الجزم بذلك لأن الهيثمي ﵀ قد عهدنا منه السكوت في كثير من الأحيان عن العلة في الحديث مثل الانقطاع والتدليس ونحوذلك، ولذلك نراه نادرا ما يقول: إسناد صحيح، أو: إسناد حسن، وإنما يقول: رجاله ثقات، أوموثقون. أو: فيه فلان وهو ضعيف، أو: مختلف فيه ونحوذلك. ولذلك فلا ينبغي للعارف بهذا العلم أن يصحح أويحسن بناء على مثل تلك العبارات منه. فإذا يسر الله لنا الوقوف على إسناد الطبراني أوأبي نعيم استطعنا الحكم على الحديث بما يستحقه من رتبة. والله الموفق.
ثم وقفت على إسناده في " المعجم الكبير " للطبراني (٢٤/١٠٦/٢٨٤) فتبين أنه

Furthermore, the previously mentioned verse, “and strengthened him with forces you did not see,” confirms that the hadith is weak, because it clearly states that the victory and support came through forces that could not be seen, whereas the hadith establishes that his ﷺ victory came through a spider, which can be seen. Consider this carefully.

The most likely interpretation of the verse is that the forces were angels, not a spider or two doves. Thus al-Baghawi said in his Tafsir (4/174), commenting on the verse: “They were angels who came down and turned the faces and eyes of the disbelievers away from seeing him.”

Some hadith reports support this meaning. Abu Nu‘aym related from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr: “Abu Bakr saw a man facing the cave and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, he can see us!’ He replied, ‘No. The angels are covering us with their wings now.’ The man soon sat down facing them to urinate. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, ‘Abu Bakr, if he could see you, he would not have done that.’”

Al-Tabarani related it at length in the account of the Hijrah. Al-Haythami said (6/54): “Al-Tabarani related it. It includes Ya‘qub, who is considered good in hadith. The hadith scholar Ibn Hajar said of him: ‘Truthful; he sometimes made mistakes.’”

If there is no other flaw in the chain of transmission, then it is good. However, I cannot state that definitively, because we have often found al-Haythami silent about flaws in hadith, such as a broken chain, tadlis, and the like. That is why he rarely says, “Its chain of transmission is authentic,” or, “Its chain of transmission is good.” Instead, he says, “Its narrators are reliable,” or, “They are deemed reliable,” or, “It includes so-and-so, who is weak,” or, “There is disagreement about him,” and the like. A person familiar with this discipline should therefore not declare a hadith authentic or good based on such phrases from him. If Allah enables us to find the chain of transmission in al-Tabarani or Abu Nu‘aym, we will be able to determine the report’s proper grade. Allah is the One who grants success.

“On the night of the cave, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, commanded a tree, which grew in front of the Prophet ﷺ and concealed him. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, sent a spider, which spun its web between them and concealed the Prophet’s ﷺ face. Allah commanded two wild doves, and they came fluttering (in one copy: flapping) until they settled between the spider and the tree. Young men from Quraysh, one from each clan, came with their sticks, bows, and clubs. When they were about two hundred cubits from the Prophet ﷺ, the guide, Suraqah ibn Malik al-Mudlaji, said, ‘Look at this rock. I don’t know where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed his foot.’ The young men said, ‘You haven’t tracked him since last night.’ When morning came, he said, ‘Look in the cave!’ The men went forward, and when they were fifty cubits away, the first one looked and saw the doves, then turned back. They said, ‘What made you turn back instead of looking in the cave?’ He said, ‘I saw two wild doves at the mouth of the cave, so I knew there was no one inside.’ The Prophet ﷺ heard them and realized that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, had used them to ward them off. He prayed for them, and Allah, Exalted is He, protected them in the sanctuary, and they laid the eggs you see.”

Munkar [rejected].

Ibn Sa‘d narrated it (1/228–229), as did al-Mukhallis in al-Fawa’id al-Muntaqah (17/13/1–2), al-Bazzar in his Musnad (2/299/1741, Kashf al-Astar), al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (20/443/1082), al-‘Uqayli (346), and Khaythamah al-Atrabulusi in Fada’il…

source_units.text_ar: جَعْفَرٍ وَأَنَا أَسْمَعُ، قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّاسِبِيُّ، قَالَ: حَدَّثَنِي فُرَاتُ بْنُ السَّائِبِ عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ، عَنْ ضَبَّةَ بْنِ مِحْصَنٍ الْعَنَزِيِّ، عن عمر ابن الْخَطَّابِ ﵁ فِي قِصَّةٍ ذَكَرَهَا، قَالَ: فَقَالَ عُمَرُ وَاللهِ لَلَيْلَةٌ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَيَوْمٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عُمُرِ عُمَرَ، هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ أُحَدِّثَكَ بِلَيْلَتِهِ وَيَوْمِهِ؟ قَالَ: قُلْتُ نَعَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَالَ أَمَّا لَيْلَتُهُ فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ هارب مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ خَرَجَ لَيْلًا فَتَبِعَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، فَجَعَلَ يَمْشِي مَرَّةً أَمَامَهُ، وَمَرَّةً خَلْفَهُ، وَمَرَّةً عَنْ يَمِينِهِ، وَمَرَّةً عَنْ يَسَارِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌: «مَا هَذَا يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ مَا أَعْرِفُ هَذَا مِنْ فِعْلِكَ؟» قَالَ: يَا رَسُولُ اللهِ أذكر الرَّصَدَ فَأَكُونُ أَمَامَكَ، وَأَذْكُرُ الطَّلَبَ فَأَكُونُ خَلْفَكَ، وَمَرَّةً عَنْ يَمِينِكِ وَمَرَّةً عَنْ يَسَارِكَ، لَا آمَنَ عَلَيْكَ، قَالَ: فَمَشَى رَسُولُ اللهِ ﵌ لَيْلَتَهُ عَلَى أَطْرَافِ أَصَابِعَهُ، حَتَّى حَفِيَتْ رِجْلَاهُ، فَلَمَّا رَآهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁ أَنَّهَا قَدْ حَفِيَتْ حَمَلَهُ عَلَى كَاهِلِهِ، وَجَعَلَ يَشْتَدُّ بِهِ حَتَّى أَتَى بِهِ فَمَّ الْغَارِ، فَأَنْزَلَهُ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: وَالَّذِي بَعَثَكَ بِالْحَقِّ لَا تَدْخُلُهُ حَتَّى أَدْخَلَهُ، فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ نَزَلَ بِي قَبْلَكَ، فَدَخَلَ فَلَمْ يَرَ شَيْئًا، فَحَمَلَهُ فَأَدْخَلَهُ، وَكَانَ فِي الْغَارِ خَرْقٌ فيه حيات وأفاعي، فَخَشِيَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْهُنَّ شَيْءٌ يُؤْذِي رَسُولَ اللهِ ﵌، فَأَلْقَمَهُ قَدَمَهُ فَجَعَلْنَ يَضْرِبْنَهُ وَيَلْسَعْنَهُ: الْحَيَّاتُ وَالْأَفَاعِي، وَجَعَلَتْ دُمُوعُهُ تَنْحَدِرُ وَرَسُولُ الله ﵌، يَقُولُ لَهُ: يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ! لَا تَحْزَنْ، إِنَّ اللهَ مَعَنَا، فَأَنْزَلَ الله سكينته الاطمئنانية لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ، فَهَذِهِ لَيْلَتُهُ.

He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Rasibi told us; he said: Furat ibn al-Sa’ib narrated to me from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Dabba ibn Mihsan al-‘Anazi, from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, in an account he related. ‘Umar said: “By Allah, one night and one day of Abu Bakr’s are better than ‘Umar’s whole lifetime. Would you like me to tell you about his night and his day?” I said, “Yes, Commander of the Faithful.” He said: “As for his night, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Makkah, fleeing its people, he went out at night, and Abu Bakr followed him. He would walk sometimes ahead of him, sometimes behind him, sometimes to his right, and sometimes to his left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘What is this, Abu Bakr? I don’t usually see you behave like this.’ He replied, ‘Messenger of Allah, I think of those lying in wait, so I go ahead of you; then I think of those pursuing us, so I go behind you. At times I go to your right and at times to your left. I cannot feel safe for you.’ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked that night on the tips of his toes until his feet were sore. When Abu Bakr saw that his feet were sore, he carried him on his shoulders and hurried with him until he reached the mouth of the cave. He set him down, then said, ‘By the One who sent you with the truth, you will not enter it until I have entered it first. If there is anything inside, it will harm me before you.’ He went in and saw nothing, then carried him in. There was a hole in the cave containing snakes and vipers. Abu Bakr feared that something might come out and harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he plugged it with his foot. The snakes and vipers began striking and biting him, and his tears streamed down as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, ‘Abu Bakr, do not grieve; Allah is with us.’ Allah sent down His tranquility upon Abu Bakr. This was his night.”

The flaws in the report:
(1) ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Rasibi.
Imam al-Dhahabi listed him in *Al-Mizan* (2/545), entry (4804), then said:
“‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Rasibi, reporting from Malik, brought a long, false report, for which he is the one accused. He also reported from Furat ibn al-Sa’ib, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Dabbah ibn Muhsin, from Abu Musa, the story of the cave—and it resembles the fabrications of storytellers.”
I say: Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar affirmed Imam al-Dhahabi’s statement about the story of the cave, that it resembles the fabrications of storytellers, in *Lisan al-Mizan* (3/491), entry (602/4953).
(2) Furat ibn al-Sa’ib.
Imam al-Dhahabi listed him in *Al-Mizan* (3/341), entry (6689), then said: “Furat ibn al-Sa’ib, reporting from Maymun ibn Mihran.”
Al-Bukhari said: “His hadith is rejected.”
Ibn Ma‘in said: “He is nothing.”
Al-Daraqutni and others said: “He is abandoned.”
Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: “Regarding Maymun, he is close to Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Tahhan in that he is accused of the same things as him.” I say: Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar affirmed Imam al-Dhahabi’s statement in *Lisan al-Mizan* (4/503–504), entry (11/6522), then said: “Abu Hatim al-Razi said: ‘His hadith is weak; his hadith is rejected.’ Al-Saji said: ‘They abandoned him.’ Al-Nasa’i said: ‘His hadith is abandoned.’”
I say: Al-Nasa’i’s statement about Furat, “his hadith is abandoned,” is cited in *Al-Du‘afa’ wa al-Matrukin*, entry (488). The statement of Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in *Sharh al-Nukhbah*, p. 69, is sufficient for you: “It was the position of Al-Nasa’i not to abandon a man’s hadith until everyone agreed to abandon it.”

source_units.text: he said: In the mountain called Thawr, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr stayed for three nights.

source_units.text_ar:
سوى ذلك، والعلماء كلهم يطلقون على ذلك قدوم المدينة. وفي شرف المصطفى لابن الجوزي عن ابن عباس ﵄ قال: ولد رسول الله ﷺ يوم الإثنين، واستنبئ يوم الإثنين، ورفع الحجر يوم الإثنين، وخرج مهاجرا من مكة يوم الإثنين، وقدم المدينة يوم الإثنين، وقبض يوم الإثنين. وفي روضة الأقشهري: قال ابن الكلبي: خرج من الغار ليلة الإثنين أول يوم من ربيع الأول، وقدم المدينة يوم الجمعة لاثنتي عشرة ليلة خلت منه. قال أبو عمر: وهو قول ابن إسحاق إلا في تسمية اليوم. وعند أبي سعيد في شرف المصطفى من طريق أبي بكر بن حزم: قدم لثلاث عشرة من ربيع الأول، وهذا الجمع بينه وبين الذي قبله بالحمل على الاختلاف في رؤية الهلال. وعنده من حديث عمر: ثم نزل على بني عمرو بن عوف يوم الإثنين لليلتين بقيتا من ربيع الأول، ولعل الرواية خلتا ليوافق ما تقدم. ونقل ابن زبالة عن ابن شهاب أن ذلك كان في النصف من ربيع الأول، وقيل:
كان قدومه في سابعه، وجزم ابن حزم بأنه خرج من مكة لثلاث ليال بقين من صفر، وهذا يوافق قول هشام بن الكلبي إنه خرج من الغار ليلة الإثنين أول يوم من ربيع الأول، فإن كان محفوظا فلعل قدومه قباء كان يوم الإثنين ثامن ربيع الأول، وإذا ضم ذلك إلى ما سيأتي عن أنس أنه أقام بقباء أربع عشرة ليلة خرج منه أن دخوله المدينة نفسها كان لاثنين وعشرين منه، لكن الكلبي جزم بأنه دخلها لاثنتي عشرة خلت منه؛ فعلى قوله تكون إقامته بقباء أربع ليال فقط، وبه جزم ابن حبان؛ فإنه قال: أقام بها الثلاثاء والأربعاء والخميس، يعني وخرج يوم الجمعة، فلم يعتد بيوم الخروج، وكذا قال موسى بن عقبة: إنه أقام فيهم ثلاث ليال؛ فكأنه لم يعد يوم الدخول ولا الخروج. وعن قوم من بني عمرو بن عوف أنه أقام فيهم اثنين وعشرين يوما، حكاه ابن زبالة. وفي البخاري من حديث أنس «أقام فيهم أربع عشرة ليلة» وهو المراد في رواية عائشة بقولها «بضع عشرة ليلة» وقال موسى بن عقبة عن ابن شهاب: أقام فيهم ثلاثا، قال: وروى ابن شهاب عن مجمع بن حارثة أنه أقام اثنتين وعشرين ليلة. وقال ابن إسحاق: أقام فيهم خمسا، وبنو عمرو بن عوف يزعمون أكثر من ذلك. قال الحافظ ابن حجر: أنس ليس من بني عمرو بن عوف؛ فإنه من الخزرج، وقد جزم بأربع عشرة ليلة، فهو أولى بالقبول، وأمر النبي ﷺ بالتاريخ فكتب من حين الهجرة في ربيع، رواه الحاكم في الإكليل، وهو معضل، والمشهور أن ذلك كان في خلافة عمر ﵁، وأن عمر قال: الهجرة فرقت بين الحق والباطل، فأرخ بها، وابتدأ من المحرم بعد إشارة علي وعثمان ﵄ بذلك، وقد ذكرنا ما قيل في
source_units.speaker_ar: السمهودي؛ مصادره المسماة في النص وتعقيبه

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَجَهَّزْنَاهُمَا أَحَثَّ الْجَهَازِ، وَصَنَعْنَا لَهُمَا سُفْرَةً فِي جِرَابٍ، فَقَطَعَتْ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قِطْعَةً مِنْ نِطَاقِهَا، فَرَبَطَتْ بِهِ عَلَى فَمِ الْجِرَابِ، فَبِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَتْ ذَاتَ النِّطَاقِ،
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري

source_units.text_ar: «صَنَعْتُ سُفْرَةَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ حِينَ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُهَاجِرَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ قَالَتْ: فَلَمْ نَجِدْ لِسُفْرَتِهِ وَلَا لِسِقَائِهِ مَا نَرْبِطُهُمَا بِهِ فَقُلْتُ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: وَاللهِ مَا أَجِدُ شَيْئًا أَرْبِطُ بِهِ إِلَّا نِطَاقِي قَالَ: فَشُقِّيهِ بِاثْنَيْنِ فَارْبِطِيهِ: بِوَاحِدٍ السِّقَاءَ وَبِالْآخَرِ السُّفْرَةَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَلِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَتْ ذَاتَ النِّطَاقَيْنِ.»
source_units.speaker_ar: أسماء في صحيح البخاري

questions.prompt: Who brought the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr news each night of what Quraysh were saying and planning?

options.text: ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr's freedman
options.feedback: ‘Amir's task was the flock: he brought the sheep to the cave for milk and drove them off before dawn.

options.text: ‘Abdullah, Abu Bakr's son
options.feedback: Right. He listened to Quraysh all day in Makkah, kept every word in his head, and came back to the cave after dark.

options.text: Asma, Abu Bakr's daughter
options.feedback: Asma brought them food each evening; the news of Quraysh's plans came with her brother ‘Abdullah.

options.text: ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, the hired guide
options.feedback: The guide did not come until the morning after the third night, bringing the camels for the road.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr's son ‘Abdullah was their ears in Makkah: among Quraysh by day, at the cave with the news by night.

questions.prompt: How did ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah help the two in the cave?

options.text: He brought a flock of milking sheep to the cave after nightfall.
options.feedback: Right. He grazed the sheep among Makkah's shepherds by day, and at night the two slept with fresh milk.

options.text: He brought them word of what Quraysh were planning.
options.feedback: That was ‘Abdullah's task; ‘Amir's part was the flock and its milk.

options.text: He kept their riding camels hidden near the mountain.
options.feedback: The camels came with the guide on the morning after the third night; ‘Amir looked after the sheep.

questions.explanation: ‘Amir, Abu Bakr's freedman, grazed his flock unnoticed among the shepherds and brought it to the cave each night for milk.

questions.prompt: How did ‘Abdullah keep Quraysh from suspecting he was in touch with the two in the cave?

options.text: He slept in Makkah and slipped out to the cave only by day.
options.feedback: It was the reverse: by day he was in Makkah listening, and he spent his nights in the cave.

options.text: He spent each night in the cave and was back in Makkah by morning.
options.feedback: Right. He left in the last hours before dawn, so he was among Quraysh in the morning as if he had slept there.

options.text: He never went to the cave himself, but sent word through Asma.
options.feedback: ‘Abdullah went to the cave himself each night; Asma brought food, not his news.

questions.explanation: By leaving the cave before dawn and appearing in Makkah each morning, ‘Abdullah seemed never to have left the city.

questions.prompt: When Abu Bakr saw the searchers' feet above him, what did the Prophet ﷺ answer to his fear?

options.text: "Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their third?"
options.feedback: Right. Abu Bakr feared one man looking down would see them, and the Prophet ﷺ answered with these words.

options.text: "Move back into the dark of the cave, so they cannot see us."
options.feedback: The Prophet ﷺ gave no plan for hiding; his answer turned Abu Bakr to Allah being with them.

options.text: "They will soon tire of searching and go back to Makkah."
options.feedback: The searchers did give up, but the Prophet's ﷺ answer was about Allah being their third, not about the searchers.

questions.explanation: With the searchers close enough to hear, the Prophet ﷺ calmed Abu Bakr: "what do you think of two when Allah is their third?"

questions.prompt: The Quran says Allah sent His tranquility "upon him" in the cave. On whom did Ibn ‘Abbas say it came down?

options.text: On Abu Bakr, for the Prophet ﷺ had never been without it
options.feedback: Right. It was Abu Bakr who was overcome with worry, and Ibn ‘Abbas held that the calm came down on him.

options.text: On the Prophet ﷺ, to steady him as the searchers came near
options.feedback: Some said this, but Ibn ‘Abbas held it meant Abu Bakr, since the Prophet ﷺ had never been without tranquility.

options.text: On the searchers, so that they turned back without looking
options.feedback: The tranquility came on one of the two in the cave; the searchers were turned away by forces no one saw.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was the one afraid, and Ibn ‘Abbas explained that the tranquility came down on him, since the Prophet ﷺ always had it.

questions.prompt: What happened on the morning after the third night?

options.text: The guide came to the cave with their two camels and a third of his own.
options.feedback: Right. ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit came as arranged, and Asma brought their bag of food for the road.

options.text: ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr brought the camels from Abu Bakr's house.
options.feedback: ‘Abdullah brought news each night; the camels came with the hired guide, ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit.

options.text: The searchers came back to the mountain for a second look.
options.feedback: The searchers had given up and gone back, and by the third night the talk about the two had died down.

questions.explanation: Once the talk in Makkah died down, the guide arrived as arranged with the camels, and the road to Madinah lay open.

questions.prompt: Most reports give three nights in the cave. Which account has, in one version, two days and two nights?

options.text: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr's account, as recorded by al-Bayhaqi
options.feedback: Right. One version of ‘Urwah's account has two days and two nights, while Musa ibn ‘Uqbah's version has three.

options.text: ‘Aishah's account in al-Bukhari
options.feedback: ‘Aishah's account is the main source for three nights: they hid in a cave in Mount Thawr "three nights".

options.text: Ibn Ishaq's biography
options.feedback: Ibn Ishaq agrees with ‘Aishah, Mujahid and al-Zuhri in giving three nights.

questions.explanation: Three nights is the reading of ‘Aishah, Ibn Ishaq, Mujahid and al-Zuhri; only one version of ‘Urwah's account has two.

questions.prompt: Abu Bakr's words in the cave reach us through Anas. How does al-Bukhari's wording of his fear differ from Muslim's?

options.text: Al-Bukhari: one might "lower his gaze"; Muslim: one might look "at his feet".
options.feedback: Right. Both describe the same fear of being seen, in different words; the story follows Muslim's.

options.text: Al-Bukhari: one might look "at his feet"; Muslim: one might "lower his gaze".
options.feedback: The wordings are swapped: "lower his gaze" is al-Bukhari's, and looking "at his feet" is Muslim's.

options.text: Al-Bukhari: one might "raise his foot"; Muslim: one might look "at his feet".
options.feedback: "If one of them raised his foot" comes from another chain recorded by al-Bayhaqi, not al-Bukhari.

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr told of the scene and Anas passed it on; al-Bukhari has "lower his gaze", Muslim "at his feet", and al-Bayhaqi "raised his foot".

questions.prompt: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar called the spider's web report hasan (good). Why did al-Albani judge it weak?

options.text: One narrator, ‘Uthman al-Jazari, was weak, and the verse speaks of forces unseen.
options.feedback: Right. He faulted ‘Uthman al-Jazari, and argued that a spider's web is not a force "you did not see".

options.text: It came bundled with the story of the tree and the two pigeons.
options.feedback: The tree and pigeons belong to a different, longer report, which al-Albani judged rejected on its own.

options.text: It appears only in late biographies, not in any hadith collection.
options.feedback: The report of Ibn ‘Abbas is recorded by Ahmad; al-Albani's objection was to a narrator and to the verse.

questions.explanation: The web rests on Ibn ‘Abbas's report in Ahmad; graded good by Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar, it was judged weak by al-Albani.

questions.prompt: When ‘Abdullah walked back to Makkah each morning, how were his footprints hidden?

options.text: ‘Amir drove the sheep along his trail, wiping out his tracks.
options.feedback: Right. The flock heading back to graze trampled ‘Abdullah's footprints, leaving no trail to the cave.

options.text: He walked only in the dark, when no one could follow.
options.feedback: He did leave before dawn, but it was ‘Amir's sheep, driven along his trail, that wiped out his footprints.

options.text: The spider's web and the rocks hid any trace near the cave.
options.feedback: The web was what the searchers saw at the entrance; ‘Abdullah's tracks were covered by ‘Amir's flock.

questions.explanation: ‘Amir's flock, driven after ‘Abdullah each morning, erased the trail that could have led Quraysh to the cave.
